title: HCP — Disclosure
description: The Human Context Protocol (HCP) 2.0-draft-3 disclosure: an entry as a Context Client receives it (HCP 7.4, 7.6), shared by the hcp/* tasks. Written for this registry from the HCP 2.0-draft-3 specification text (CC BY 4.0, https://github.com/loyalagents/hcp-spec), with attribution; not copied from HCP's own schema files. Open, as HCP's objects are (HCP Appendix A.3). Where this schema and the HCP text differ, the HCP text governs.

Disclosure.description: A disclosed copy of an entry. It carries a grant-scoped `ref` in place of the entry's stable `id` (HCP 7.4), and the instant until which the client may use the copy (HCP 7.6). The entry parts it carries have the shapes the shared Entry gives them.

ref.description: The grant-scoped reference to the entry (HCP 7.4). Stable for one grant and different across grants, so two clients cannot join their copies on it.

useUntil.description: The instant after which the client MUST NOT use this copy (HCP 7.6): at least one hour and at most 30 days after disclosure, and at most 24 hours for High-sensitivity context.

classification.description: The entry's categories and purpose limits.

record.description: The entry's status and provenance as disclosed.

evidence.description: Evidence items disclosed with the entry. Absent when none is disclosed.
